issue.title: Import: an app entry with an API the existing provider lacks (same key, same host) shows Already added and its endpoint is dropped
issue.body:
Sibling of the Add fix for one key used in two formats (energetic_wolf_99424 on Discord; Add's check now also needs the new provider to bring no API, or address of one, the existing provider lacks — `servesAll` in internal/provider/provider.go).

The app import still judges "already added" by key + host + headers only (`sameProvider` in internal/provider/importapps.go, used by `settle`'s "same" status and `holds`). So when magpie has a relay as a provider with only its OpenAI endpoint (Chat), and the user imports the same relay's Claude Code entry (Anthropic endpoint, same key), the entry shows "Already added" and its Anthropic endpoint is never saved anywhere: requests keep going through the OpenAI endpoint with translation.

Not changed in the Add fix because the import deliberately treats one key at one host as one account (`merge` folds a relay's Claude Code and Codex entries into one provider with two endpoints, #1486). The likely fix is to fold the missing endpoint into the existing provider on import (or offer it), not to add a second provider. Not reproduced with a real import yet.

comments.body:
Root cause: the app import judged "already added" by `sameProvider` alone — key + host + headers (`settle`'s "same" status, `holds`) — which is exactly the check the Add form had before its fix for one key used in two formats taught it `servesAll`. So a relay magpie holds with only its OpenAI endpoint (Chat) showed the same relay's Claude Code entry (same key, same host, Anthropic endpoint) as "Already added", and the Anthropic endpoint was never saved anywhere: requests kept going through the OpenAI endpoint with translation.

Fix: the import keeps treating one key at one host as one account (#1486) and now folds the missing endpoint into the provider that holds it, as `merge` folds one account's two entries within one source — not a second provider, which stays the Add form's answer for two formats.

- `bringsAPI(h, p)`: the entry names an address of an API the holder is asked at none of its own for. A same-kind address only spelled differently (…/v1 beside the bare host) brings nothing and keeps the old "same".
- `settle`: such an entry is offered ("new"), not "Already added"; re-settled after the fold it says "same" again.
- `ImportFromApps`: the endpoints the holder lacks are copied in and the holder is saved; the added list names it "Entry (Holder)", as adding a key does.

`TestGeminiURLIsItsHost`'s import half moved with the contract: a Chat entry at a Gemini-only relay is offered and folds — the relay is still known by its Gemini URL's host — while its Gemini-only half still says "same".

Verification:
- New regression tests, red on clean main: `TestImportEntryWithAPITheProviderLacks` (settle unit) and `TestImportFoldsTheEndpointItBrings` (full flow over a temp HOME's Claude Code settings.json — entry "Already added", Anthropic endpoint never saved before; after the fix one provider holds both endpoints and re-settles to "same").
- `go test ./internal/provider/` (all, including the updated Gemini test) and `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gui/` pass; gofmt/vet/build clean.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/4904-import-folds-endpoint (ef20298d2)

Boundary: endpoints only — the entry's models, headers and keys are not folded (its key is the holder's already, by sameProvider); hidden providers and signed-in accounts never receive folds. Not tried: a real import from a real relay, and a browser walkthrough of the picker row the offered entry now gets. As the issue notes it was not reproduced with a real import: the test drives the same reader (`readClaudeSettings`) with a fake settings.json.

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.
